Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] GlobalProtect successful login from CVE-2026-0257 pre-PoC exploitation IPs · [LLM] GlobalProtect connection with PoC-spoofed host-ID, MAC, or device name · [LLM] GlobalProtect connection with PoC client fingerprint: Win10 Pro 64-bit + empty d · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] GlobalProtect successful login from CVE-2026-0257 pre-PoC exploitation IPs Exploitation High
Hunts successful GlobalProtect portal/gateway sessions sourced from the nine IPs Unit 42 attributed to pre-PoC (before 2026-05-29) exploitation of the PAN-OS authentication bypass CVE-2026-0257. Any successful tunnel from these origins is a high-confidence foothold indicator. Rationale: Uses the nine source IPs Unit 42 explicitly attributed to pre-PoC (pre-2026-05-29) exploitation of CVE-2026-0257 against GlobalProtect portals/gateways. A successful gateway-connected event from any of these IPs is a direct foothold indicator. Falcon/CloudWatch empty because GlobalProtect VPN logs do not ship to FDR or CloudWatch Logs natively. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/active-exploitation-of-pan-os-cve-2026-0257/

[LLM] GlobalProtect connection with PoC-spoofed host-ID, MAC, or device name Exploitation High
Alerts on successful GlobalProtect gateway-connected events whose host-id or machine name matches the placeholder MACs (aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff, 00:11:22:33:44:55) or generic device names (WINDOWS-LAPTOP-001, DESKTOP-GP01, GP-CLIENT) hard-coded by the public PoC for CVE-2026-0257. These identifiers should not appear in any legitimate corporate VPN client. Rationale: Targets the exact five placeholder identifiers Unit 42 published: two patently-fake MACs (aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff is the canonical example MAC; 00:11:22:33:44:55 is a sequence-pattern placeholder) and three generic Windows device names baked into the PoC. Defender query is intentionally a corroboration baseline against DeviceInfo — if those device names never legitimately exist in the estate, any VPN log referencing them is definitively spoofed. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/active-exploitation-of-pan-os-cve-2026-0257/
ATT&CKT1078 T1556 T1133
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| summarize LastSeen = max(Timestamp), DeviceCount = dcount(DeviceId) by DeviceName
| where DeviceName in~ ("WINDOWS-LAPTOP-001","DESKTOP-GP01","GP-CLIENT")
| project DeviceName, LastSeen, DeviceCount
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Palo Alto Networks"
| where DeviceProduct has_any ("GlobalProtect", "PAN-OS")
| where Activity has_any ("gateway-connected", "GlobalProtect connected", "portal-auth-succ")
| where Message has_any ("aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff", "00:11:22:33:44:55", "WINDOWS-LAPTOP-001", "DESKTOP-GP01", "GP-CLIENT")
   or SourceHostName in~ ("WINDOWS-LAPTOP-001","DESKTOP-GP01","GP-CLIENT")
   or SourceMACAddress in~ ("aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff","00:11:22:33:44:55")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, SourceHostName, SourceMACAddress, Activity, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: GlobalProtect Connection With PoC-Hardcoded Client Identifiers (CVE-2026-0257)
id: 9c2c7d05-1a4f-4b3c-8b22-5f1e9e0d2202
description: Detects GlobalProtect gateway-connected events using the placeholder MAC addresses or generic device names hard-coded in the public PoC for CVE-2026-0257.

NETWORK
`pan_globalprotect` (event_id="gateway-connected" OR event_id="GlobalProtect connected" OR log_subtype="gateway-connect")

[LLM] GlobalProtect connection with PoC client fingerprint: Win10 Pro 64-bit + empty d Exploitation Medium
Hunts post-PoC-release GlobalProtect gateway-connected events whose endpoint_os_version field equals 'Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 64-bit' AND whose source_user_info.domain field is empty — the hard-coded client fingerprint left in the public PoC for CVE-2026-0257. Domain-joined corporate endpoints almost never present an empty domain. Rationale: Targets the exact two hard-coded PoC client-configuration values Unit 42 published for post-2026-05-29 hunting: endpoint_os_version literal 'Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 64-bit' AND empty source_user_info.domain. Sentinel regex uses a verbatim @-string so backslashes do not collide with JSON/KQL string escaping (fix for prior validation error). Defender query is an environment baseline — local-only Win10 Pro hosts that would plausibly emit an empty domain. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/active-exploitation-of-pan-os-cve-2026-0257/
ATT&CKT1078 T1556 T1133
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where OSPlatform =~ "Windows10" and OSVersion has "Pro"
| where isempty(LoggedOnUsers) or LoggedOnUsers !has "domain"
| summarize LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, JoinType
| where JoinType !in~ ("AzureAD","Hybrid","Domain")
| project LastSeen, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, JoinType
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Palo Alto Networks"
| where DeviceProduct has_any ("GlobalProtect", "PAN-OS")
| where Activity has_any ("gateway-connected", "GlobalProtect connected")
| where Message has "Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 64-bit"
| where Message matches regex @"(?i)source_user_info\.domain\s*[:=]\s*(?:,|;|$|\s)"
   or Message matches regex @"(?i)domain\s*[:=]\s*(?:,|;|$|\s)"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, SourceHostName, DestinationIP, Activity, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:pan_os (@evt.name:gateway-connected OR @evt.name:"GlobalProtect connected") @endpoint_os_version:"Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 64-bit" (-@source_user_info.domain:* OR @source_user_info.domain:"")
APPLICATION
`pan_globalprotect` (event_id="gateway-connected" OR event_id="GlobalProtect connected" OR log_subtype="gateway-connect")
    endpoint_os_version="Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 64-bit"
    (source_user_info.domain="" OR NOT source_user_info.domain=*)
| stats earliest(_time) as firstTime latest(_time) as lastTime values(src_ip) as src_ips values(host_id) as host_ids values(machine_name) as machines count by src_user endpoint_os_version
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| where count >= 1
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-0257")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-0257")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-0257")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-0257")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'

            - '\chrome.exe'

level: high

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e") or SHA1 in~ ("6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e") or MD5 in~ ("6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e") or SHA1 in~ ("6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e") or MD5 in~ ("6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442") or SHA1 in~ ("524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442") or MD5 in~ ("524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442") or SHA1 in~ ("524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442") or MD5 in~ ("524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442"]);
union

        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,

    ( ImProcessCreate

        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,

Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] OP-512 Potato Suite SYSTEM escalation from IIS worker (SeImpersonate token abuse) · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — New Threat Cluster OP-512 Targets Microsoft IIS Servers with Custom Web Shell Fr
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] IIS worker w3wp.exe writes .aspx/.ashx handler to upload/temp directory (OP-512 web shell drop)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] OP-512 C2 beacon to ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com from IIS host · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] IIS w3wp.exe spawns whoami /priv or cmd.exe — OP-512 web shell command execution · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] OP-512 C2 beacon to ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com from IIS host Command & Control High
Detects DNS resolutions or HTTP egress to the OP-512 attacker-controlled domain ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com observed in the ReliaQuest report. Article-specific because this domain appeared ~75 days before the main intrusion as the initial staging beacon and is reused by the web shell's self-reporting fallback over DNS/HTTP. Rationale: The domain ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com is the only network IOC named in the ReliaQuest write-up; matching it across DNS and HTTP egress is a definitive OP-512 signal. Cross-checked the IOC pattern via the article's lead and MITRE T1071.004 mapping. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where RemoteUrl has "lhlsjcb.com" or RemoteUrl has_cs "ashx.lhlsjcb.com"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp asc
let ioc_domain = "lhlsjcb.com";
(union isfuzzy=true
    (DnsEvents
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
        | where Name has ioc_domain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, ClientIP, Domain = Name, QueryTypeName, Source = "DnsEvents"),
    (ImDnsActivity
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
        | where DnsQuery has ioc_domain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, ClientIP = SrcIpAddr, Domain = DnsQuery, QueryTypeName = DnsQueryTypeName, Source = "ImDnsActivity"),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
        | where RequestURL has ioc_domain or DestinationHostName has ioc_domain or DestinationDnsDomain has ioc_domain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = SourceHostName, ClientIP = SourceIP, Domain = coalesce(DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain), URL = RequestURL, Source = "CommonSecurityLog")
)
| order by TimeGenerated asc

[LLM] IIS worker w3wp.exe writes .aspx/.ashx handler to upload/temp directory (OP-512 web shell drop) Installation High
Detects the IIS worker process w3wp.exe writing ASP.NET handler files (.aspx, .ashx, .asmx) into upload or temp directories — the exact drop pattern ReliaQuest observed for the OP-512 three-shell framework. Combines parent-process (w3wp.exe) and target-extension predicates to keep false positives down on legitimate deployment activity. Rationale: ReliaQuest explicitly names w3wp.exe as the process that dropped the web shell into the application's upload directory. The parent (w3wp.exe) + extension (.aspx/.ashx) + path (upload/temp) triple gives strong specificity to OP-512 vs legitimate publish flows. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190

DeviceFileEvents

| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where FileName endswith ".aspx" or FileName endswith ".ashx" or FileName endswith ".asmx" or FileName endswith ".asax"
| where FolderPath has_any ("\\upload", "\\uploads", "\\temp", "\\tmp", "\\App_Data", "\\images", "\\files")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RequestSourceIP
| order by Timestamp desc

| where ActingProcessName has "w3wp.exe"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("aspx", "ashx", "asmx", "asax")
   or TargetFileName endswith ".aspx"
   or TargetFileName endswith ".ashx"
   or TargetFileName endswith ".asmx"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("\\upload", "\\uploads", "\\temp", "\\tmp", "\\App_Data", "\\images", "\\files")
| project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: IIS w3wp.exe Writes ASP.NET Handler to Upload or Temp Directory
id: 8a2e5d11-7b40-4c5b-9f8a-3d5b6e0c8e21
description: Detects the IIS worker process w3wp.exe creating ASP.NET handler files (.aspx/.ashx/.asmx/.asax) in upload, temp, or App_Data directories — the OP-512 web shell drop pattern.
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05

logsource:

| ContextImageFileName=/\\w3wp\.exe$/i
| TargetFileName=/\.(aspx|ashx|asmx|asax)$/i
| regex("\\\\(upload[s]?|temp|tmp|App_Data|images|files)\\\\", field=TargetFileName, flags="i")

ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name="w3wp.exe" (Filesystem.file_name="*.aspx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.ashx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.asmx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.asax") (Filesystem.file_path="*\\upload*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\uploads*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\temp*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\tmp*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\App_Data*") by host Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] IIS w3wp.exe spawns whoami /priv or cmd.exe — OP-512 web shell command execution Actions on Objectives High
Detects the IIS worker w3wp.exe spawning interpreter or reconnaissance binaries (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, whoami.exe, net.exe) — directly matching ReliaQuest's observed OP-512 post-exploitation step of running whoami /priv from the web shell to confirm SYSTEM-level privileges after Potato Suite escalation. Rationale: ReliaQuest directly cites whoami /priv as the post-Potato verification command from OP-512, and the entire chain hinges on w3wp.exe being the parent. Parent (w3wp.exe) + child (recon binaries) is exactly the article's described observed sequence. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1033/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.003 T1033 T1087
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "whoami.exe", "net.exe", "net1.exe", "systeminfo.exe", "ipconfig.exe", "tasklist.exe", "hostname.exe", "wmic.exe", "reg.exe", "sc.exe")
| extend IsWhoamiPriv = (FileName =~ "whoami.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/priv", "/all", "/groups"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, IsWhoamiPriv
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe"
| extend ChildName = tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1])
| where ChildName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "whoami.exe", "net.exe", "net1.exe", "systeminfo.exe", "ipconfig.exe", "tasklist.exe", "hostname.exe", "wmic.exe", "reg.exe", "sc.exe")
| extend IsWhoamiPriv = (ChildName =~ "whoami.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("/priv", "/all", "/groups"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType, IsWhoamiPriv
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: IIS Worker w3wp.exe Spawns Recon Binary (OP-512)
id: 4f7b3c6a-2d11-4f8d-8a51-7e2b1a4c9e3f
description: Detects w3wp.exe spawning cmd/powershell/whoami/net/systeminfo as a child, consistent with OP-512 web shell post-exploitation reconnaissance after Potato Suite SYSTEM escalation.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-threat-cluster-op-512-targets.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
    - attack.t1505.003
    - attack.t1059.003
    - attack.t1033
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
status: experimental
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\whoami.exe'
            - '\net.exe'
            - '\net1.exe'
            - '\systeminfo.exe'
            - '\ipconfig.exe'
            - '\tasklist.exe'
            - '\hostname.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\reg.exe'
            - '\sc.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - IIS web apps that legitimately shell out to net.exe / ipconfig.exe for diagnostics endpoints (rare)
level: high
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) (@EventID:4688 OR @EventID:1) @ParentImage:(*\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE) @Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.EXE OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\whoami.exe OR *\WHOAMI.EXE OR *\net.exe OR *\net1.exe OR *\systeminfo.exe OR *\ipconfig.exe OR *\tasklist.exe OR *\hostname.exe OR *\wmic.exe OR *\reg.exe OR *\sc.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^w3wp\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|whoami|net1?|systeminfo|ipconfig|tasklist|hostname|wmic|reg|sc)\.exe$/i
| WhoamiPriv := if(ImageFileName=/whoami\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/\/(priv|all|groups)/i, "true", "false")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=[count(), min(@timestamp)])
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="w3wp.exe" (Processes.process_name="cmd.exe" OR Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" OR Processes.process_name="pwsh.exe" OR Processes.process_name="whoami.exe" OR Processes.process_name="net.exe" OR Processes.process_name="net1.exe" OR Processes.process_name="systeminfo.exe" OR Processes.process_name="ipconfig.exe" OR Processes.process_name="tasklist.exe" OR Processes.process_name="hostname.exe") by host Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="w3wp.exe" (Processes.process_name="cmd.exe" OR Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" OR Processes.process_name="pwsh.exe" OR Processes.process_name="whoami.exe" OR Processes.process_name="net.exe" OR Processes.process_name="net1.exe" OR Processes.process_name="systeminfo.exe" OR Processes.process_name="ipconfig.exe" OR Processes.process_name="tasklist.exe" OR Processes.process_name="hostname.exe") by host Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] OP-512 Potato Suite SYSTEM escalation from IIS worker (SeImpersonate token abuse) Exploitation High
Detects token-impersonation privilege escalation from the IIS app-pool identity to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM — the exact Potato Suite (RottenPotato/JuicyPotato/GodPotato/RoguePotato) chain ReliaQuest observed after OP-512 dropped its web shells. Pivots on child of w3wp.exe with integrity-level jump to System, plus Windows 4672 'special privileges' assignments to non-service accounts. Rationale: ReliaQuest explicitly names the Potato Suite as OP-512's escalation tool from the IIS app-pool to SYSTEM. The IIS-worker-as-parent plus Potato binary-name keywords plus integrity-level jump make this a high-fidelity escalation indicator. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1134/001/ • https://github.com/ohpe/juicy-potato • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
ATT&CKT1134.001 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let PotatoFingerprints = dynamic(["juicypotato", "rottenpotato", "sweetpotato", "godpotato", "roguepotato", "localpotato", "remotepotato", "printspoofer", "efspotato"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where ProcessIntegrityLevel in~ ("System", "High")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any (PotatoFingerprints)
   or FileName has_any (PotatoFingerprints)
   or InitiatingProcessTokenElevation =~ "TokenElevationTypeFull" and AccountName =~ "SYSTEM" and InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("system", "network service", "local service")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessIntegrityLevel, ProcessTokenElevation, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
let PotatoNames = dynamic(["juicypotato", "rottenpotato", "sweetpotato", "godpotato", "roguepotato", "localpotato", "remotepotato", "printspoofer", "efspotato"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe"
| extend ChildName = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where TokenElevationType in ("%%1936", "%%1937")  // Full or Default-elevated
   or CommandLine has_any (PotatoNames)
   or ChildName has_any (PotatoNames)
   or (SubjectUserSid == "S-1-5-18" and ParentProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, SubjectUserSid, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Potato Suite Privilege Escalation from IIS w3wp.exe
id: 9e3c12b8-1d6a-44e9-bf7c-2c0a3b8e15dc
description: Detects Potato-family (Juicy/Rotten/Sweet/God/Rogue/Local/Remote/PrintSpoofer/EFS) privilege escalation invoked from the IIS worker w3wp.exe, matching OP-512's observed SYSTEM escalation.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-threat-cluster-op-512-targets.html
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1134/001/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
    - attack.t1134.001
    - attack.t1068
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
status: experimental
detection:
    parent_iis:
        ParentImage|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'
    potato_keywords:
        - CommandLine|contains:
            - 'juicypotato'
            - 'rottenpotato'
            - 'sweetpotato'
            - 'godpotato'
            - 'roguepotato'
            - 'localpotato'
            - 'remotepotato'
            - 'printspoofer'
            - 'efspotato'
        - Image|contains:
            - 'potato'
            - 'printspoofer'
    condition: parent_iis and potato_keywords
falsepositives:
    - Authorized red team engagements
level: critical
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) (@EventID:4688 OR @EventID:1) @ParentImage:(*\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE) (@CommandLine:(*juicypotato* OR *JuicyPotato* OR *rottenpotato* OR *RottenPotato* OR *sweetpotato* OR *SweetPotato* OR *godpotato* OR *GodPotato* OR *roguepotato* OR *RoguePotato* OR *printspoofer* OR *PrintSpoofer* OR *efspotato* OR *EfsPotato*) OR @Image:(*potato* OR *Potato* OR *POTATO* OR *printspoofer* OR *PrintSpoofer*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^w3wp\.exe$/i
| (regex("(?i)(juicypotato|rottenpotato|sweetpotato|godpotato|roguepotato|localpotato|remotepotato|printspoofer|efspotato)", field=CommandLine)
   OR regex("(?i)(potato|printspoofer)", field=ImageFileName)
   OR IntegrityLevel="System")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, IntegrityLevel], function=[count(), min(@timestamp)])
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.process_integrity_level) as integrity from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="w3wp.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_path="*\\inetsrv\\w3wp.exe") (Processes.process_integrity_level="System" OR Processes.process_integrity_level="high") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="SYSTEM" OR process_name!="w3wp.exe" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.process_integrity_level) as integrity from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="w3wp.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_path="*\\inetsrv\\w3wp.exe") (Processes.process_integrity_level="System" OR Processes.process_integrity_level="high") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="SYSTEM" OR process_name!="w3wp.exe" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"

     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.

Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents

[LLM] Everest Forms Pro RCE exploit attempt from named source IPs Delivery High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests to vulnerable WordPress sites from the four IPv4 sources Wordfence attributed to the CVE-2026-3300 exploitation campaign. Highest fidelity signal since the IPs were named in the original advisory and have driven 29,300+ blocked attempts since 2026-04-13. Rationale: Wordfence's named source IPs are the highest-confidence pivot in the article. Combining IP source + WordPress admin-ajax/everest_forms URI keeps the false-positive surface near zero. Cross-checked with Wordfence's advisory and abuse.ch ThreatFox for IP reputation. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wordfence.com/blog/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/

[LLM] Everest Forms Pro Calculation Addon PHP injection payload in form submission Exploitation Medium
Hunts POST bodies to WordPress endpoints containing PHP code-context characters that escape sanitize_text_field() and reach eval() in process_filter(). Targets the specific injection shape described by Wordfence — single quotes followed by PHP functions like system, exec, base64_decode, or backticks. Rationale: Wordfence quotes the bug as 'concatenating user-submitted form field values into a PHP code string without proper escaping before passing it to eval()' — the discriminating signal is PHP-function tokens (system, exec, base64_decode, shell_exec, assert) plus single-quote-break characters in a POST to admin-ajax/everest_forms. Cross-checked the wp-json everest path against the Everest Forms plugin source. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wordfence.com/blog/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web

| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-fpm.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("admin-ajax.php","everest_forms")
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("system(","exec(","passthru(","base64_decode","shell_exec","assert(","'.system")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where csMethod == "POST"
| where csUriStem has_any ("admin-ajax.php","everest_forms","wp-json")
| where csUriQuery has_any ("system(","exec(","passthru(","base64_decode","shell_exec","assert(","%27.system","%27%2Bsystem","`","%60")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus),
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| where RequestURL has_any ("admin-ajax.php","everest_forms","wp-json")
| where Message has_any ("system(","exec(","passthru(","base64_decode","shell_exec","assert(","'.system","'+system")
   or RequestCookies has_any ("system(","base64_decode")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, Message),
(AppServiceHTTPLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where CsMethod == "POST"
| where CsUriStem has_any ("admin-ajax.php","everest_forms")
| where CsUriQuery has_any ("system(","exec(","base64_decode","shell_exec","'.system")
| project TimeGenerated, CsHost, CIp, CsMethod, CsUriStem, CsUriQuery, UserAgent, ScStatus)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] WordPress rogue 'diksimarina' admin account creation request Installation High
Hunts the specific payload Wordfence saw most commonly in CVE-2026-3300 exploitation: creation of a WordPress administrator account named 'diksimarina' with email 'diksimarina@gmail.com'. Hardcoded IOCs from the original advisory. Rationale: 'diksimarina' and 'diksimarina@gmail.com' are verbatim IOCs from Wordfence's report cited in the article — extremely high-fidelity strings unlikely to appear organically in benign traffic. Searching across multiple log surfaces (WAF, IIS, App Service, syslog) catches the payload regardless of where it lands. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wordfence.com/blog/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1136/001/

[LLM] WordPress PHP worker spawning shell or download utility post-RCE Installation Medium
Hunts the post-exploit behaviour where the PHP/Apache/Nginx worker process spawns sh, bash, wget, curl, python, perl, or nc — the natural follow-on after process_filter() eval() succeeds and the attacker drops a webshell or pulls a second-stage payload. Rationale: The article's kill-chain note explicitly cites 'PHP/Apache/Nginx worker processes spawning unusual children (sh, curl, wget)' as the execution-phase pivot. Pairing the parent web-tier binary with download/shell child binaries follows the BluRaven process-tree pattern and avoids the anti-bare-process-execution smell. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1505.003 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php-fpm7.4","php-fpm8.0","php-fpm8.1","php-fpm8.2","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","wget","curl","python","python3","perl","nc","ncat","socat","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","wget","curl","python","python3","perl","nc","ncat","socat","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","certutil.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine),
(SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-cgi.exe","php.exe","w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine),
(Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Facility =~ "authpriv" or ProcessName has_any ("audit","auditd")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("php-fpm","apache2","nginx","httpd")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/bin/sh","/bin/bash","/usr/bin/wget","/usr/bin/curl","/usr/bin/python","/usr/bin/perl","/usr/bin/nc")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 6f4e8b3a-1c92-4d57-8a4b-3b7e2c1d9e44
status: experimental
description: Detects PHP/Apache/Nginx worker processes spawning unix shells, curl/wget, python/perl, or nc - high-confidence post-RCE indicator on WordPress hosts following CVE-2026-3300 or similar PHP eval() exploitation.
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:

logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/php-fpm'
      - '/php-fpm7.4'
      - '/php-fpm8.0'
      - '/php-fpm8.1'
      - '/php-fpm8.2'
      - '/httpd'
      - '/apache2'
      - '/nginx'
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\php-cgi.exe'
      - '\php.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/wget'
      - '/curl'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/perl'
      - '/nc'
      - '/ncat'
      - '/socat'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) (@ParentImage:(*\php-cgi.exe OR *\php.exe OR *\w3wp.exe OR *\httpd.exe OR *\nginx.exe) OR @process.parent.executable.path:(*/php-fpm* OR */httpd OR */apache2 OR */nginx)) (@Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe) OR @process.executable.path:(*/sh OR */bash OR */wget OR */curl OR */python* OR */perl OR */nc OR */ncat OR */socat))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(php-fpm|php-cgi|php|httpd|apache2|nginx|w3wp)/i
| ImageFileName=/(\/sh|\/bash|\/dash|\/wget|\/curl|\/python3?|\/perl|\/nc|\/ncat|\/socat|\\cmd\.exe|\\powershell\.exe|\\certutil\.exe|\\bitsadmin\.exe)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-3300")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-3300")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("a7eadcf81dd6fda0dd6affefaffcb33b1d8f64ddec6e5a1772d028ef2a7da0f2", "58e17dd61d4d55fa77c7f2dd28dd51875b0ce900c1e43b368b349e65f27d6fdd", "e1fc59c7ece6e9a7fb262fc8529e3c4905503a1ca44630f9724b2ccc518d0c06", "8ee4ec425bc0d8db050d13bbff98f483fff020050d49f40c5055ca2b9f6b1c4d", "9c745f95a09b37bc0486bf0f92aad4a3d5548a939c086b93d6235d34648e683f", "e512d22d2bd989f35ebaccb63615434870dc0642b0f60e6d4bda0bb89adee27a") or SHA1 in~ ("a7eadcf81dd6fda0dd6affefaffcb33b1d8f64ddec6e5a1772d028ef2a7da0f2", "58e17dd61d4d55fa77c7f2dd28dd51875b0ce900c1e43b368b349e65f27d6fdd", "e1fc59c7ece6e9a7fb262fc8529e3c4905503a1ca44630f9724b2ccc518d0c06", "8ee4ec425bc0d8db050d13bbff98f483fff020050d49f40c5055ca2b9f6b1c4d", "9c745f95a09b37bc0486bf0f92aad4a3d5548a939c086b93d6235d34648e683f", "e512d22d2bd989f35ebaccb63615434870dc0642b0f60e6d4bda0bb89adee27a") or MD5 in~ ("a7eadcf81dd6fda0dd6affefaffcb33b1d8f64ddec6e5a1772d028ef2a7da0f2", "58e17dd61d4d55fa77c7f2dd28dd51875b0ce900c1e43b368b349e65f27d6fdd", "e1fc59c7ece6e9a7fb262fc8529e3c4905503a1ca44630f9724b2ccc518d0c06", "8ee4ec425bc0d8db050d13bbff98f483fff020050d49f40c5055ca2b9f6b1c4d", "9c745f95a09b37bc0486bf0f92aad4a3d5548a939c086b93d6235d34648e683f", "e512d22d2bd989f35ebaccb63615434870dc0642b0f60e6d4bda0bb89adee27a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["a7eadcf81dd6fda0dd6affefaffcb33b1d8f64ddec6e5a1772d028ef2a7da0f2", "58e17dd61d4d55fa77c7f2dd28dd51875b0ce900c1e43b368b349e65f27d6fdd", "e1fc59c7ece6e9a7fb262fc8529e3c4905503a1ca44630f9724b2ccc518d0c06", "8ee4ec425bc0d8db050d13bbff98f483fff020050d49f40c5055ca2b9f6b1c4d", "9c745f95a09b37bc0486bf0f92aad4a3d5548a939c086b93d6235d34648e683f", "e512d22d2bd989f35ebaccb63615434870dc0642b0f60e6d4bda0bb89adee27a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GHOST STADIUM FIFA lookalike domain resolution (fifa.bio/.center/.gold/.red/.sale/.shopping/.show/.ski) Delivery High
Detects DNS resolution or HTTP connection from corporate or employee endpoints to the specific FIFA World Cup 2026 lookalike domains attributed to GHOST STADIUM. Hits indicate a user followed a Facebook ad, Telegram/WhatsApp link or SEO result into the cloned PingIdentity SSO phishing kit. Rationale: Domain list is the exact GHOST STADIUM cluster registered since August 2025 (per Group-IB tracking cited in the article). These are not legitimate FIFA properties — fifa.com is the only legitimate root — so any internal endpoint resolving them is high-fidelity initial-access signal. Cross-checked against the kill-chain Phase 1 IOCs. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/fifa-world-cup-2026-scams-are-already.html

[LLM] GHOST STADIUM phishing kit / Android trojan C2 IP egress (8 specific hosts) Command & Control High
Detects outbound connections from any internal endpoint (workstation, mobile via NAT, server) to the eight IP addresses that host the cloned fifa.com phishing infrastructure and serve as C2 for the Massiv/Perseus Android banking trojans. Article-specific IP set, not a reputation feed. Rationale: These are the exact infrastructure IPs Group-IB enumerated for the GHOST STADIUM cluster cited in the article. Eight discrete /32 destinations — small enough to enumerate, large enough to span the cloned-site fleet and the trojan C2. Any internal-to-IP connection is high-signal because none of these IPs front legitimate enterprise services. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/fifa-world-cup-2026-scams-are-already.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1437.001 T1583.004

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteIP in (GhostStadiumC2)

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol

[LLM] Massiv / Perseus (Cerberus-derived) Android banking trojan APK hash on managed endpoint Installation High
Detects the three specific SHA1 hashes of the trojanised RojaDirecta-style streaming APKs distributed alongside the World Cup 2026 fraud campaign. Matches against any file-write or download channel (browser saves, MDM-relayed install records, USB transfers) where the bytes touch a corporate-managed device. Rationale: These three SHA1 hashes are explicitly named in the kill-chain Phase 2 IOCs as the Massiv/Perseus APKs. SHA1 collisions across legitimate software are vanishingly rare; the APK extension + streaming-themed filename adds defense in depth for catching repacks even if the exact hash drifts. Highest-confidence host-side signal in the campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/fifa-world-cup-2026-scams-are-already.html

| where SHA1 in (MassivPerseusHashes) or (FileName endswith ".apk" and (FileName has_any ("roja","directa","fifa","worldcup","stream","futbol","soccer")))
